intent: Let the owner give an approved commit a release name.

edit.summary:
I added a `name_release` action to `authoring/authoring.domain.yaml`. It lets the owner give an approved commit a release name.

- **New field:** `Commit` now has an optional `release_name` string.
- **New action:** `name_release` is owner-only and needs a person. It takes a `release_name` and sets it on the commit. A precondition, `approved-to-name`, allows it only on a commit with `approved == true`.
- **Transitions:** I added `name_release` to the `Commit` matrix as `recorded → recorded`.
- **Version:** I raised the domain version from 15 to 16.

The new action, its precondition and its matrix entry are marked `status: proposed`, because the request gave no interview source to cite. I didn't add a scenario for it. I didn't change the delivery domain or the composition, so the release name isn't passed to Delivery.

I also left the request silent on two points, so the action allows both. The owner can rename a commit that already has a release name. Nothing stops two commits from sharing a name.

findings.problem: name_release writes release_name onto a Commit that is already approved. The glossary says a commit is an immutable snapshot, that every change is a new commit and that nothing is edited in place. cite_evidence and record_check also treat an approved commit as settled. The new action changes an approved commit in place and can be repeated, so a release name can be silently overwritten. The glossary and the Commit description are not updated to say that release_name is mutable metadata, and nothing stops a second rename.

Nothing constrains the name. An empty string is accepted, although skip_stage rejects an empty reason, and that would wipe a name. Two commits can share the same name, which defeats the stated purpose of referring to a release instead of a commit id. There is no uniqueness check, no rename guard and no format rule.

The release name stays in Authoring and is not carried to Delivery. The deliver_approved_commit handoff passes only the commit id, and Delivery's DeliveryRequest and Environment still identify releases by commit id, so people see the id again in Delivery. The glossary has no 'release name' entry either.

findings.problem: The new action has no scenario and no world fixture exercising it. For example, naming the approved commit C1 should work, and naming the unapproved C2 should be denied by approved-to-name. The action, its precondition and its matrix cell are all status 'proposed' with no source or interview citation, so the permission and approval semantics are untested and unconfirmed.

name_release sets release_name on an existing Commit. That contradicts the rule that a commit is an immutable snapshot and that nothing is edited in place. It also conflicts with the settled-commit rules: check_commit and cite_evidence deny changes to an approved commit, and the glossary says approval cannot be undone. name_release is the only action that changes an approved commit's own record, and nothing reconciles this, either by updating the glossary and description or by storing the name outside the commit.

The owner can silently rename a release or point one name at several commits, which defeats the purpose of referring to a release instead of the commit id. A repeat call is allowed by the matrix and nothing checks for it.
release_name is an unconstrained string, so an empty or blank name is accepted. skip_stage guards its free-text reason with `params.reason != ''`, but name_release has no equivalent check.

The release name is not carried anywhere that people look at releases. The deliver handoff to Delivery passes only the commit id, so DeliveryRequest and Delivery's Environment still identify what is deployed by commit id. The stated goal of talking about releases rather than commit ids is therefore not met downstream. The change also adds no scenario or fixture covering name_release, including the denial on an unapproved commit.

It also conflicts with the rules that treat an approved commit as settled: check_commit not-approved, record_check settled, and cite_evidence not-approved. The release name can be silently reassigned, and nothing stops two commits from having the same name.

findings.problem: release_name has no non-empty check, unlike skip_stage, which requires params.reason != ''. An owner can set an empty release name, which defeats the purpose of referring to a release by name.

The name stays on the Authoring Commit only. The deliver handoff to Delivery still carries just the commit id, and DeliveryRequest and Environment have no release name. The people who deliver and verify therefore still see commit ids, which is the problem the change set out to fix. Nothing says whether a name given after delivery is shown anywhere in Delivery.

The new action and field have no scenario, no fixture with a release_name, and no glossary entry for 'release' or 'release name'. The rule that only an approved commit can be named (approved-to-name) and the rule that only owners can name one are never exercised. The C1 fixture is approved and could have been used to test them.

name_release is limited to owner, while approve_commit also allows the deputy, so a deputy who approves a commit while the owner is away cannot name the release. findings.problem: The new action has no scenario and no fixture. The existing approved commit C1 is unused, and there is no check that an unapproved commit such as C2 or C3 is denied by approved-to-name. The rule and the new matrix cell are untested. The action, its precondition and its matrix cell are all marked status: proposed, with no source or interview citation.

name_release has no rule against reusing a release name or renaming a commit. Two commits can get the same release name, and an approved commit's name can be overwritten at any time. The purpose is that people refer to a release by its name instead of the commit id, so a name that is ambiguous or can move to another commit defeats that. The sibling actions enforce 'once' with a precondition or a deny cell (decide, fetch_source, approve_commit), but this one has neither.
release_name is a free string with no non-empty check. An empty name can be set, which looks like a name but identifies nothing. skip_stage already guards against this with params.reason != ''.

The release name is never passed on when the commit is delivered. The deliver_approved_commit handoff and Delivery's DeliveryRequest still carry only the commit id, so Delivery and anything downstream of it still talk in commit ids. This leaves the stated reason for the change ('people talk about releases, not commit ids') only partly met.

The glossary says a commit is an immutable snapshot and that nothing is edited in place. Cite_evidence says an approved commit is 'settled'. name_release now changes a field on an already-approved commit. The glossary has no entry for a release name, and its description of approval and commits does not say that a name can be added or changed afterwards.

No scenario covers name_release, neither the denial on an unapproved commit nor naming an approved one. The new precondition and the new matrix cell are untested, even though the world has both an approved commit (C1) and unapproved ones (C2, C3) ready to use.
